fix(cli): force UTF-8 stdout/stderr to fix Windows crash on non-ASCII output

On Windows, sys.stdout/sys.stderr inherit the console's codepage
(commonly cp1252) unless explicitly reconfigured. Any streamed model
output containing a character outside that codepage (arrows, box
drawing, emoji, etc.) raised UnicodeEncodeError inside print mode,
which surfaced as a confusing double failure: a wrapped
typer.BadParameter box, plus an unrelated-looking asyncgen
RuntimeError from the abandoned provider stream's GC cleanup.

Reconfigure both streams to UTF-8 as early as possible at import time,
tolerating streams that don't support .reconfigure() (e.g. some
test/CI capture streams).

fix(google): round-trip thoughtSignature on Gemini tool calls

Gemini 3 models attach a "thoughtSignature" to each functionCall part
in the response, and require it echoed back on the next turn or every
subsequent request fails with:

  Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts.

tau captured tool calls from the stream but discarded this signature,
so any multi-turn conversation that used a tool (i.e. almost all of
them) broke immediately after the first tool call.

- Add an optional `thought_signature` field to the shared `ToolCall`
  model (ignored by every other provider).
- Capture `thoughtSignature` off streamed functionCall parts in
  `_GoogleStreamParser.feed`.
- Replay it back as a sibling `thoughtSignature` key when rebuilding
  the assistant turn in `_message_to_google`.

Note: this complements #288 (Gemini `additionalProperties` schema
fix). Verified live end-to-end against the real Gemini API with both
fixes applied together — a prompt using the `bash` tool completed
successfully across multiple turns.

fix(google): strip unsupported JSON Schema keywords from tool params

Gemini's function-calling API only accepts an OpenAPI-3.0 subset of
JSON Schema and rejects requests containing "additionalProperties"
(or "$schema") with a 400 error. tau forwarded tool input schemas to
Gemini unmodified, so any request that included a tool (which is
effectively every request) failed immediately.

Recursively strip these keys from tool parameter schemas before
sending them to Gemini.

fix(session): walk session tree iteratively to prevent /tree crash on long sessions

Invoking `/tree` on a long session raised "RecursionError: maximum
recursion depth exceeded". `_ordered_tree_entries` ordered entries with a
recursive helper that recursed once per tree depth, so a session whose
root-to-leaf entry chain was longer than Python's recursion limit (~1000)
overflowed the stack. A malformed parent cycle recursed forever as well.

Replace the recursion with an explicit-stack depth-first walk that
preserves the exact traversal order and terminates on cycles via an
`expanded` guard, so `/tree` works on arbitrarily long sessions.

fix: resolve release-notes crash by bundling releases.json inside the package

The published wheel never included release-notes/releases.json despite the
artifacts config in pyproject.toml — Hatch's wheel target ignores artifacts.
On first launch after an upgrade, startup_release_notes_notice() called
load_release_notes() and crashed with FileNotFoundError because the file was
missing from disk. On a second launch the version check exited early (state
file was updated during the crashed run), masking the bug.

Move releases.json inside src/tau_coding/data/ so it becomes regular package
data, auto-bundled by Hatch with no special config.  This also eliminates the
layout-dependent path resolution: Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'data' /
'release-notes' / 'releases.json' now resolves identically in both dev
(source tree) and installed (site-packages) layouts, removing the need for
importlib.resources or a parents[2]/parents[1] fallback.

* fix: make test_coding_session pass on Windows

Two problems broke 4 tests for every Windows contributor:

* Fix: extension key interceptors must run pre-dispatch, ahead of app priority bindings

The component seam spliced the extension key interceptor into the top of
PromptInput.on_key. That is too late and too narrow: tau binds
down/up/tab/alt+enter on the App with priority=True, and Textual's
App.on_event runs _check_bindings(priority=True) BEFORE forwarding a key to
the focused widget. So a focused widget (and the interceptor splice inside it)
never sees those nav keys — completion_next/previous/accept fire first. A
widget-owned nav model is therefore impossible under tau's app-priority
bindings, which is why the subagents strip's keyboard switching never worked.

Port pi's onTerminalInput as a true pre-dispatch hook: override
TauTuiApp.on_event and, for a non-forwarded events.Key, consult the extension
key interceptors before calling super() (hence before the priority bindings
and the focused widget). Interceptors are consulted only on the main screen
(len(screen_stack) <= 1) so modal dialogs/pickers/command palette keep owning
their keys, and only when one is registered so the default path is untouched.
Remove the now-redundant splice from PromptInput.on_key.

Because interceptors now see every main-screen key regardless of focus, they
must self-gate — documented on register_key_interceptor (bridge + protocol)
and in the design doc's 2e implementation note. Adds core tests: a
priority-bound key (down) is interceptable, and keys are not intercepted while
a modal screen is open.

optimistically without its custom_type/details and then discarded the
confirming event, and the mid-run drain dropped the metadata in

the registered card.

would double-render if expansion ever rewrote the payload) and render once
from the confirmed user event, which carries the metadata; the incremental
append path resolves and threads custom_markup so the first paint — and the

The UserMessage custom-metadata serializer exists so sessions that never
use extensions stay readable by old extra="forbid" binaries — but

harness it built before _persist_loaded_interrupted_tool_repairs(),

dangling tool call. Loading such a session (e.g. resuming after being
killed mid-tool-call) left extensions subscribed to the discarded
harness, so they silently received zero agent events.

* Replace the optimistic prompt render when an input hook transforms it

The optimistic dedupe requires exact equality between the typed text and
the confirmed UserMessage content. An extension input hook with
action="transform" rewrites plain typed text inside session.prompt —
exactly the text that is optimistically rendered — so the confirmed
event fell through to _append_confirmed_user_message and both the
original and transformed texts rendered permanently. Rewrite the run's
optimistic item in place instead.

lived in the app with no teardown seam, so it survived /resume and

construction despite its comment — and /reload leaked interceptors,
accumulating one copy per reload while stale slot widgets stayed

frontend). The runtime drives it from reset_for_reload, and

session_start so handlers can re-mount into a clean frontend. A
pending main-view wait() resolves with None, honoring the handle's
documented rebind semantics.

reconciles instead of un-awaited remove() calls outside the locks, so
a clear followed by an immediate same-id re-mount cannot hit

recurring failure is visible again in the new world.

TauTuiApp.on_click refocused the prompt after every left click in the main

conversation viewer). The view takes focus on mount, so its keys worked only
until the first click anywhere — after which esc, ctrl+o, and typed text all
silently rerouted to the main chat. Skip the refocus while a main view is
open; clicking the prompt itself still focuses it via Textual's native

Cache Anthropic prompts instead of re-billing every turn (#502)

* Cache Anthropic prompts instead of re-billing every turn

Tau placed no cache_control breakpoints at all, so every request re-billed the
system prompt, the whole tool schema block, and the entire conversation as fresh
input. The usage side was already wired up — cache_read, cache_write and
ephemeral_1h_input_tokens were parsed and priced — but nothing ever asked the API
to cache, so those counters read zero on every real turn and a long coding
session cost roughly an order of magnitude more input than it needed to.

Spend all four breakpoints Anthropic allows: the last tool, the final system
block, this request's tail, and the previous request's tail. Only the final
system block is marked because a breakpoint on the OAuth identity block would
cache a prefix the block after it already covers. Two message positions rather
than one because the API checks at most 20 block positions back from a
breakpoint, and one tau turn appends 2N+2 blocks for N tool calls, so a wide
parallel-tool turn falls out of that window; marking where the previous request
ended opens a second lookback window there. That position is reconstructed from
the payload rather than tracked across requests: the transcript is append-only
and every request stops immediately before the assistant message it produces,
so the last user message before the final assistant turn is exactly where the
previous tail breakpoint sat.

Retention is a tri-state on AnthropicConfig. Subscription OAuth asks for the 1
hour TTL, since it is not billed per token and the 5 minute default is shorter
than a test run or a diff review — verified against the live API that OAuth
honors ttl=1h rather than silently downgrading. API-key auth keeps the 5 minute
default so nobody pays 2x for cache writes they did not ask for. The four
catalog providers that speak the Anthropic protocol through a gateway
(minimax, minimax-cn, fireworks, vercel-ai-gateway, one of which proxies to
non-Anthropic models) opt out entirely, so they keep receiving the exact payload
they received before, plain-string system field included.

The session sidebar now reports a cache hit rate, which is the only way to tell
this is working without watching a rate limit. It stays hidden for providers
that never report cache usage at all rather than showing a permanent 0%.

* Document Anthropic prompt caching

Add the contributor note under dev-notes/ covering how the four breakpoints are
allocated and why, how the previous-request boundary is reconstructed from the
payload rather than tracked across requests, why retention differs by auth type,
and how to validate the behavior end to end.

On the docs site, record the sidebar's new cache hit rate and how to read a low
one, and explain in the providers guide that subscription OAuth asks for the one
hour cache while an API key keeps the five minute default, and that the four
gateway providers speaking the Anthropic protocol send no breakpoints at all.

* Copy cache_control per breakpoint and cover the negative paths

_cache_control returned a single dict that was attached by reference to the
system block, the last tool, and both message breakpoints. It is serialized
immediately so nothing is wrong today, but mutating one marker later would have
silently changed all four. Copy at each attach site.

Add the tests that were missing their negative half: the cache hit rate is
hidden rather than shown as 0% when no provider reported cache activity, and
Copilot's Anthropic-protocol models opt out of breakpoints like the other
gateways do.

* Make prompt-cache capability overridable via compat

Cache retention was derived entirely in code from base-URL host and auth mode,
with no way for a user to change it. That is fine until Anthropic changes its
mind: an unsupported ttl is a hard 400 invalid_request_error, tau does not retry
400s, so if ttl=1h ever stops being honored on subscriptions every request fails
and the only fixes are editing source or switching auth. The same gap blocks the
opposite case, where someone points the Anthropic provider at a caching-capable
proxy and silently loses caching.

Split capability from intent. Intent stays in code — OAuth wants the 1 hour TTL,
an API key wants the shorter default. Capability moves to three compat booleans
resolved through the existing detected -> provider -> per-model layering, the same
path forceAdaptiveThinking already takes on this provider: supportsCacheControl,
supportsLongCacheRetention, and supportsCacheControlOnTools. Capability only ever
narrows intent, so the two compose without a precedence rule and there is no
"did the user set this" check to get wrong.

Two of those keys were already in the catalog with nothing reading them —
_detected_compat emitted supportsLongCacheRetention, and the Fireworks model
entries declare both it and supportsCacheControlOnTools, mirrored in from Pi.
This makes that data live instead of adding a parallel vocabulary, and picking
booleans over a retention string also removes any question of validating an
unrecognized value.

The hostname rule becomes a detected default rather than a hard rule, so every
existing gateway keeps its current behavior while becoming overridable. Also
fixes the openai-compatible anthropic-messages branch, which hardcoded no
caching and ignored compat entirely — that path serves Copilot's Claude models,
real Claude behind a proxy, and so was the one most likely to want the override.

fix: Persist interrupted tool results with push-based persistence (#526)

* Persist interrupted tool results with push-based persistence

When the TUI cancelled the worker consuming session.prompt() mid-tool-
call, the synthetic "Tool call interrupted by user" result was appended
only to the in-memory harness: the persist step after the event loop
never ran on teardown, and later count-based watermarks silently
classified the orphan as already persisted. The session file was left
with assistant(tool_use) and no tool result, which providers reject.

Modeled on Pi's architecture: persistence now subscribes to harness
events (message_end is the durable boundary) instead of running in the
generator consumer, so consumer teardown cannot lose writes. The harness
finally-block now notifies subscribers of the synthetic repairs it
appends on cancellation, with listener failures suppressed so they
cannot mask the in-flight cancellation. Count watermarks are removed; an
identity-keyed reconcile in prompt()/continue_() retries persists whose
message_end fired but whose write failed.

* Document push-based persistence in dev-notes

Adds dev-notes/push-based-persistence.md, updates the durable-message
boundary section in design/04-sessions.md, and corrects the interrupted
tool-call roadblock resolution in tui-coding-agent-footprint.md, which
described the cleanup repair as recovering persisted sessions when it
was in-memory only.

* Trim comments to essentials

* Relate push persistence to Pi's implementation in dev-notes

* Route entry-path tool-call repairs through events

A persist failure could kill a run after the assistant tool call was
persisted but before its result was. The repair at the next run start
then synthesized the missing result without events, so it entered
provider context but never reached the session file — the same dangling
tool_use corruption through a different door. Moving the repair into
_run emits message_start/message_end, so push persistence writes it.

* Tidy push-based-persistence dev-note

* Harden push persistence retries and event order

* Read durable entry ids only when retrying a persist

A first persist attempt mints message and leaf ids that cannot already be on
disk, so the idempotency read was pure overhead on the streaming path: every
message paid a second full session-file read and parse on top of the state
refresh. Gate the read on the retry path and pin the clean-run cost with a
counting-storage test.

fix: Resolve prompt completions at the caret position (#522)

* Resolve @file completions at the cursor position

The completion helpers put the caret at the end of the text. Because of
this, @file suggestions only appeared for the last token of the prompt.

Pass the cursor offset into build_completion_state. Find the mention
token that contains the cursor. Match on the text before the cursor.
Replace the full token on accept. Put the caret after the inserted
mention.

* Add CompletionItem.cursor_after_apply helper

Replace the two inline caret computations in app.py. The helper keeps
the caret math next to apply().

* Resolve shell path completions at the cursor position

Shell path suggestions assumed the caret at the end of the text. Resolve
the token at the caret. Match on the text before the caret. Replace the
full token on accept.

Decline completion when the token tail holds shell syntax. A replacement
there could splice a path into quoting. Clamp the forward scan for a
trailing backslash.

* Refresh prompt completions when the caret moves

The completion popup only updated on text edits. A caret move into a
file mention did not show suggestions. A caret move away kept a stale
span that an accept could splice at the wrong offsets.

Rebuild the completion state on TextArea.SelectionChanged.

* Stop the mention token at any whitespace

The token-end scan only stopped at a space or a newline. A tab after
the mention was replaced on accept, which removed text. Use isspace()
to match the shell token scan.

* Skip file suggestions that equal the existing token

The shell path branch already skips these. Without the skip, a finished
mention keeps an open popup, and Enter rewrites the prompt instead of
submitting it. The popup now also closes after an accept.

* Open completions only from edits, not caret moves

A caret move into a complete mention opened the popup. Enter then
rewrote the mention instead of submitting the prompt. A caret move now
only updates or clears an open popup. Typing stays the only way to open
it.

* Pin Enter submit with the caret in a complete mention

This is the regression from review. The popup stays closed, and Enter
submits the prompt.

* Pump the event loop before the caret park in the submit test

Without the pause, the queued Changed handler reads the parked caret
and opens the popup. Real typing processes the edit first.

* Close completions on caret moves instead of rebuilding

A caret move now only closes the popup once the caret leaves the completed
token, deferred until after an edit's Changed rebuild, so typing no longer
walks the file tree twice per keystroke. Drop the shell-syntax tail check and
trim overlapping cursor tests.
